title: Shuffle Abernathy's band and Burke Bailey's quartet in Milwaukee
summary: Thomas played in Shuffle Abernathy's band at Eagle's Ballroom before 3,500 people and in Bailey's four-piece cabaret group across the river.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. A helluva band. We worked in Millwaukee, we worked in Eagle's Ballroom. I thought it was a tremendous band and I was fortunate enough through this same Burke Bailey to I was ready double I'd say in around 2 years/to leave there. So the last ... Burke had another job across the river.

Burke Bailey, please remember his name because he's a tremendous person. So, we worked out there for something like Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays, Sunday afternoon and Sunday night. So I said, I thank for making (...) so I got to make it so he gave me the whole deal out for me. You can make it this way. You can get make it here, here, here, you know. And sometimes your up days after the upbeat were from Saturday to Sunday because when you start on a saw them on Saturday night, you don't sleep any more until maybe Tuesday morning ...
You mean this was working two gigs?
You mean one was Shuffle Abernathy and one was with Burke Bailey?

Yes. But, Shuffle Abernathy might be the name you remember but Burke Bailey had a lot of things to do with ... And, he had a lot of things to do with the things I had to do so sometimes Saturday afternoon, Saturday night we'd start ... OK, fine and we worked Sunday afternoon at the Eagle's.
Eagle's Ballroom. And we played to around 3500 people.
Now the Eagle's Ballroom is the gig with ...
Abernathy. This is a big band.
And Burke Bailey's is a small group.
Around four pieces. WD: Across the river.
